question: Does finite-width end contact change force and rotation relative to centerline contact on exactly the same conforming 3D solid?
scope: Local inclined thin-wall cantilever mechanism test, not G, not replacement of its XY/free macro boundary conditions.
base: z=0 clamped U1/U2/U3; U2=0 throughout for plane strain along extrusion
loading: Rigid horizontal top platen, U3=-.2mm; other rigid DOFs fixed; frictionless direct hard node-to-surface contact
solver: JAX-FEM installed Newton with scipy spsolve, local static only
changed_factor: Only node membership/tributary area of secondary top contact surface; all solid nodes, elements, material, loading and constraints identical.
measurements: Full reaction-displacement curve, external work, displacement, end rotation from deformed cross-section, eccentricity of contact normal force, reaction balance and penetration.
difference_denominator: Full cap result at same displacement; RMS normalized by full-cap maximum load. Signed cap/rim difference also report relative rim at endpoint.
causal_working_gate: If full-cap force differs by >5% of rim at endpoint with matching loading, <1e-3 relative reaction imbalance and contact penetration<1e-4mm, contact support has a material effect in this benchmark. No transfer of magnitude to G.
volume_mesh: conforming affine HEX27 4x1x40; 27 volume Gauss points, same physical solid as prior C3D20R benchmark
occupancy: rho=1 at all volume points; shared objective_void energy reduces exactly to matched NH
case_nodal: 23 Abaqus top-node locations with identical total/equal nodal area, duplicate element occurrences divided, penalty versus Abaqus direct hard contact
case_gauss: Original JAX-FEM 3x3 face Gauss sampling per top face, same reference-area penalty form as current G
changed_factors_between_JAX_cases: Only surface sampling/weights; same material, HEX27 volume, BC, kn and static increments. C3D20R versus HEX27 and penalty versus direct contact remain explicit differences to Abaqus.
comparison: 0-2%,201 samples, fixed Abaqus full-cap maximum denominator for RMS; endpoint bias JAX/Abaqus-1, displacement vectors at identical physical nodes; no fitted constants
working_gate: Endpoint absolute bias <=5%, RMS/Abq cap maximum <=5%, positive actual J, equilibrium residual<=2e-9 N; provisional local check, no mesh convergence certification
